title: Configuration Boolean encoding
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine, let $C,n,s$ be natural numbers, let $x$ be a Boolean string, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $x$. If $x$ has length $n$, encode the bits of its configuration row as a Boolean word of length $C(s+n+1)$. If $x$ does not have length $n$, use the all-false Boolean word of that length.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
$c$ is a configuration of $M$ on input $x$
caveat: The valid-length branch depends on the bounded configuration-code construction referenced in the supplied definitions.
